To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the radio emission from air showers is strongly influenced by the lateral particle distribution, the energy and the angular distributions of the particles, the energy distribution of the electrons and that the temporal distribution of the radio emission is determined by the electron energy distribution.

the use of histograms in CORSIKA simulations of air showers leads to an increase of the radio emission by up to an order of magnitude, that this increase is due to the improved description of the lateral and temporal particle distribution in the shower front and that the emission is strongly enhanced in the case of showers with large lateral particle distributions.

the radio pulse shape of extensive air showers is determined by the energy spectrum of the primary particle and by the geomagnetic field, while its amplitude depends on the geomagnetic field strength, the energy spectrum of primary particles and the zenith angle of the shower.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the simulation of the radio emission from extensive cosmic ray air showers.
the simulation of the radio emission of extensive air showers.
the simulation of radio emission from cosmic ray extensive air showers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the time being, the parametrisation-based simulation strategy is still the best choice, but that the histogram-based strategy is the better one for the future.

the new code allows to simulate radio emission from air showers in an even more realistic way, but that it is not yet clear whether it will lead to a significantly different interpretation of the measured data.
, in general, the new CORSIKA-simulation-based approach gives a better agreement with the measured data than the old one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a more realistic air-shower model leads to more realistic predictions of the radio emission.
the new code allows a more detailed analysis of the radio emission, and that the results obtained with the new code differ from those obtained with the old code, but not significantly.
the use of histograms instead of parametrisations leads to a more accurate description of the particle distributions, and hence to a more accurate prediction for the radio emission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a more realistic CORSIKA air shower simulation leads to significant changes in the simulated radio emission from air showers.

the radio emission is not very sensitive to the details of the air shower model, but that the new histograms are a useful improvement, in particular for showers of lower energy and/or with a smaller core distance.
the radio emission from air showers is very sensitive to the details of the shower development.
